name: Section Flow Pitch Deck
description: Strict section-based Q&A flow with 10 enforced sections.

questions.question: What is your company's official name?
questions.tooltip: Enter the legal or trading name you want displayed on the title slide.

questions.question: What is your company tagline or one-sentence pitch?
questions.tooltip: A catchy, short phrase that summarizes your value proposition (e.g., 'Airbnb for X').

questions.question: What is the primary problem or pain point you are solving?
questions.tooltip: Describe the specific pain your customers feel. Quantify it if possible (e.g., 'Time wasted', 'Money lost').

questions.question: Who is your primary target customer?
questions.tooltip: Select the group that most urgently needs your product.

questions.question: How does your product solve the problem described earlier?
questions.tooltip: Explain your solution simply. Focus on the benefits, not just the technology.

questions.question: What are the key features or 'vibe' of your solution?
questions.tooltip: Select the attributes that make your product stand out.

questions.question: How do people currently solve this problem without you?
questions.tooltip: Identify who or what you are replacing (e.g., competitors or manual 'Excel sheets').

questions.question: What is your current monthly revenue stage?
questions.tooltip: Be honest about your current financial traction. This builds credibility.

questions.question: How many active users or customers do you have?
questions.tooltip: Select the range that best represents your active user base.

questions.question: What is your approximate month-over-month growth rate?
questions.tooltip: Enter a percentage (e.g., '15%') or a brief description of your momentum.

questions.question: Who are the key founders and what is their relevant background?
questions.tooltip: List names and 1-2 key achievements or past companies (e.g., 'Jane Doe: Ex-Google, 10y Sales').

questions.question: Who are your direct competitors?
questions.tooltip: List the specific companies you are competing against for market share.

questions.question: How will you acquire your customers?
How much capital are you raising in this round?
questions.tooltip: Select the range that matches your fundraising goal.

questions.question: How do you plan to allocate these funds?
questions.tooltip: Briefly describe the split (e.g., '40% Engineering, 30% Sales, 30% Marketing').
